about.title: Selma Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product can hurt someone in a split second — a machine part fails on a Floral Avenue farm, a household appliance malfunctions near Highland Avenue, or a tool breaks down on a job site off Mccall Avenue. Fresno County families dealing with these injuries often assume they have to prove the manufacturer was careless. Under California law, that's usually not the case: strict liability generally means an injured person only needs to show the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. This applies whether the flaw came from how the product was designed, how it was made, or a missing warning about its risks. Manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers can share responsibility. Our team handles defective product claims in Selma and throughout Fresno County at no upfront cost, working on contingency so there's no fee unless a recovery is made.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Selma Claims

items.title: No Need to Prove Carelessness
items.desc: Because California applies strict liability to many defective product cases, an injured person generally doesn't have to show the maker was negligent — just that the product was defective and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially share liability, which matters in a supply chain that may stretch well beyond Selma or even Fresno County.

items.title: The Product Itself Is Evidence
items.desc: Preserving the defective item — whether it's equipment used along the Golden State Boulevard corridor or a household product — can be critical, and we can advise on handling it properly.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Usually not. California's strict liability rule generally means you only need to show the product had a defect — in its design, manufacturing, or warnings — and that the defect caused your injury. This is different from many other types of injury claims that require proving carelessness.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including any packaging, instructions, or broken pieces. Don't attempt repairs or modifications. We can advise on preserving evidence properly before it's lost or altered.

items.question: Does it matter that this happened in Selma?
items.answer: Local details can still matter — for example, whether the incident happened at a workplace near Highland Avenue or Mccall Avenue, or involved a product sold locally versus shipped from elsewhere. Our team familiar with Fresno County claims can help sort out where the case needs to be filed and who may be responsible.

items.question: Is there a cost to speak with us?
items.answer: No. We offer free initial consultations, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
